JPM.rationale: JPM presents a moderately attractive fundamental case anchored by strong Q1 2026 results (revenue $49.84B +10% YoY, EPS $5.94 +17.2% YoY, operating margin ~41%) and a durable #1 franchise across deposits, cards, investment banking fees, and asset management. The stock has de-rated to the floor of its 365-day valuation range (PE 13.7x, P/B 2.22x) while fundamentals improved — a clear divergence. The positively sloped yield curve (10Y-2Y spread 0.46%) and stable Fed funds rate at 3.63% support continued NII growth. However, the score is capped below +0.5 by several factors: (1) missing Q4 2025 data prevents verification of whether Q1's step-up is a genuine inflection or seasonal; (2) P/B of 2.22x is still well above the 5-year average of ~1.8x cited by Motley Fool, meaning the franchise premium is embedded even if PE has compressed; (3) Dimon's own caution at the Bernstein conference (2026-05-27) about capital markets cyclicality and the $1B expense guidance increase to ~$106B signal near-term margin headwinds; (4) elevated oil at $92.65 (+30%) and rising long-end yields introduce macro uncertainty. The Q1 beat and valuation floor provide a modest near-term rerating path, but the CEO's caution and expense revision partially offset this catalyst, warranting a score in the +0.2 to +0.5 range rather than a stronger conviction call.
